text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Croatian and Yugoslav authorities did not know about arrest and "forced extradition" of former Serb mayor of Vukovar Slavko Dokmanovic to The Hague War Crimes Tribunal, says UNTAES spokesman Philip Arnold. Yugoslav government calls for Dokmanovic's release. United Nations spokesman says this was the first such arrest in Eastern Slavonia, Croatia, but did not comment whether similar actions against war crimes suspects can be expected in Bosnia.

- Part of Serbia's opposition announces return to Serbian parliament after two-year boycott. Central topic government's draft law on local self-government which the opposition says strives for complete centralisation of power.
- Vuk Draskovic re-elected leader of Serbian Renewal Movement at third party congress.
- New Yugoslav president to be elected by July 25, 30 days after expiry of former President Zoran Lilic's mandate.
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic suspends Interior Minister Dragan Kijac, Bosnian Serb government says decision unconstitutional.
- Ruling Montenegrin Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) to decide on July 11 on candidate for republican president. Five DPS officials accepted nominations for the post.
POLITIKA

- Draft law on self-government, to be discussed by Serbian parliament at its extraordinary session, introduces proportional election system for elections of local and city councillors and the two-house Kosovo and Metohija assembly.
- Yugoslav parliamentary delegation, headed by House of Republics Vice President Radmilo Bogdanovic, on seven-day return visit to Ghana.

- Obstacles to expanding Yugoslav-Macedonian economic cooperation include unadjusted legal international regulations, lack of payments operations between the two countries and financial support from banks.
- Large stocks and poor sales force Serbia's biggest tobacco factory Duvanska Industrija Nis (DIN) to send workers on three weeks compulsory leave. DIN stocks rise to 6,500 tonnes of cigarettes.

- How funds from Serbia's Development Fund will be used. Hard currency credits for three to six months at annual interest rates of four percent for producers-exporters who have profitable programmes and secured foreign markets.
- Yugoslav air carrier JAT total 1997 income planned at $226 million, says JAT General Manager Zika Petrovic.
- Several hundred incidents registered on the Yugoslav-Albanian border over the past few years, with Yugoslav border guards most frequent victims of armed conflicts.
- One-month term for registering pirate radio and TV stations expires today, warns Yugoslav Telecommunications Minister Dojcilo Radojevic.
- Belgrade among the hottest cities in the world, together with Budapest, Tehran and New Delhi, with temperatures soaring to 35 degrees Celsius on Sunday.
BORBA

- Federal Minister Nebojsa Maljkovic said talks between Yugoslav delegation and London club of creditors last week on reprogramming more than $2 billion of Yugoslavia's debt were exhausting for both sides.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbia's Labour Office to set aside 28.8 million dinars to finance 134 programmes which will open 9,848 new jobs.
- Elektronska Industrija Nis to export $10 million worth of colour TV sets and washing machines to the United States.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- New ferry line opens between Ancona, Italy and Montenegrin port of Bar twice a week. The trip on the luxury Sansovino, with a capacity for 1,100 passengers and 24 trucks, takes 19 hours. One-way passenger ticket 130 German marks.
- There are 13,000 tourists in Budva, 7,500 of them in hotels. Room and breakfast in A category hotels now costs around 220 dinars, after July 10 310 dinars.

- In a letter to Pobjeda, Dusko Markovic, MP and general secretary of the government, refuted allegations by Mojkovac Mayor Radenko Boskovic that the government neglected economic development of the town and the northern parts of the republic in favour of the south. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311-4305
